definition: Brooding means sunk in dark, silent thought — dwelling on a trouble, turning it over and over.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word brooding. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know brooding should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: All autumn the benched quarterback grew brooding, replaying the interception on his phone long after the film sessions ended.
Pensive is milder than brooding — absorbed in thought, but the thinking can be calm, even pleasant; brooding shuts the door and turns the thought dark.
Tormented is stronger than brooding: the dark thought stops being dwelt on and starts doing the hurting, giving its owner no rest at all.

Sullen is gloom worn on the outside — the scowl, the short answers, the refusal to join in. Brooding turns the gloom inward: the dark mood has a thought at the center of it, being turned over and over.
Moody means given to shifting spells of gloom that come and go without much cause. Brooding is one dark spell with an object — a brooding person is stuck on something in particular.

The root is still a plain English noun. By June the mallard was steering her brood across the pond in a wobbling, peeping line.
Brooding means sunk in dark, silent thought — dwelling on a trouble, turning it over and over.
The novelist gave her detective a brooding streak: between cases he sat for hours over the one file he had never closed, turning its dead ends over in his mind while the tea went cold beside him.
That is the word's whole anatomy: a dark thought, held in silence, kept warm for a long time.
The image underneath is the hen on her nest — to brood is literally to sit on eggs until they hatch — and a brooding person sits on a trouble the same way.
The word also stretches to things that look heavy with something about to break: a brooding sky, a brooding castle on the cliff.
Brooding is the reviewer's word for dark interiority — a brooding hero, a brooding score, a brooding stretch of coastline.
Its unit-mate morose names settled ill-tempered gloom with no particular object; brooding always has something at its center, a trouble being sat on.
Applied to places and skies, it means they look like they're doing the same thing.
